headline: Lānaʻi residents share budget priorities with Council committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: Residents testified on the mayor's proposed budget, asking for farm support, a bigger college building, a community center and help for kūpuna.
meeting.recap: The committee's only agenda item was the mayor's proposed fiscal year budget.[[0:02:15]] A speaker for local coaches asked for money to add an extended roof and gutters to the Lānaʻi Field House.[[0:03:41]] A testifier asked for more funding for programs that help kūpuna (elders) age at home.[[0:06:45]] A farmer asked that the Lānaʻi Food Stimulus Program pay farmers more often than every six months.[[0:08:28]] She said she thinks the agriculture budget is 0.2% of the overall budget.[[0:10:39]] A college program leader said she needs a bigger building for the program to grow.[[0:17:18]] A farmer of 50 years said farming should be the number one priority.[[0:19:24]] A testifier asked for targeted funds so planning commission meetings can be held in person and on Zoom.[[0:26:36]] Another testifier asked for a community center that could also serve as an emergency shelter.[[0:38:06]] A council member said the military is looking at county land for a category five shelter, which is like a bunker.[[0:40:31]] The council member said a new affordable housing project includes a community center open to everyone.[[0:40:52]] A testifier said farmers want a commercial kitchen with a processing center and want to find funding for it.[[0:45:00]] The chair adjourned the meeting.[[0:49:18]]
meeting.next: The chair said she will share the field house sports programs proposal with staff so members can have a copy. A council member asked the college program leader for contact information to talk further.

moments.q: "That building is made to serve people and youth."
"You do not sustain the farmers, the people are going to starve."

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: A Lānaʻi farmer said more money should go into the county's food and nutrition security plan.
issues.why: A farmer said that if farmers are not sustained, people will go hungry.
issues.next: A Lānaʻi farmer said she hopes to apply for the Farm to Family Grant.
issues.brief: A Lānaʻi farmer said her sales grew 900% from 2024 to 2025.[[#1]] She said she now feeds over 400 families, partly by working with the Lānaʻi Food Pantry.[[#2]] A commercial farmer said current programs may work for backyard farmers but not for commercial farmers.[[#3]] A testifier said the composting machine farmers rely on has been down for two to three years.[[#4]]
